第 31 章 Forecasting with Less Effort and More Accuracy用更少的努力做更准确的预测

Matthew Philip / 马修·菲利普

— 第 94 页 —

When we estimate something, whether it's a batch of work or any particular single piece, the typical goal is to answer the question "When will it be done?" But do our traditional ways of estimating how long it takes to complete a task work? When we ask a group or individual to estimate knowledge work—work that by its nature is complex and unique—the information about the work is very low. Although more modern, Agile estimating practices (when done correctly) mitigate some of the pain of estimating—planning poker, for instance, is intended to reduce biases and time spent—estimating still requires time that we could spend on creating the software (opportunity cost) and involves multiple human biases. And we're still considering (and guessing at!) only a part of what accounts for delivery time: effort, or essential complication; that is, the amount of time it takes to do the job itself. Developers hate estimating, and managers hate nagging developers and missing deadlines.

当我们估算某事时——无论是一批工作还是任何单个任务——典型目标是回答「什么时候能做完？」但我们传统估算任务时长的方式有效吗？当我们让一个团队或个人估算知识工作——本质上复杂且独特的工作——时，关于工作的信息非常少。虽然更现代的敏捷估算实践（正确做的话）减轻了一些估算的痛苦——例如计划扑克旨在减少偏见和时间——但估算仍然需要我们本可以用来创建软件的时间（机会成本），而且涉及多种人类偏见。而且我们仍然只考虑（和猜测！）影响交付时间的一部分：工作量，或本质复杂度；也就是做工作本身需要的时间。开发讨厌估算，经理讨厌催开发和错过截止日期。

Fortunately, we have probabilistic forecasting. A probabilistic forecast is simply a forecast communicated as a range and a probability. For example, most weather forecasts indicate the likelihood of some event occurring, such as snowfall:

幸运的是，我们有概率预测。概率预测简单说就是以范围和概率传达的预测。例如，大多数天气预报会说明某事件发生的可能性，比如降雪：

  • No accumulation: 11%无积雪：11%
  • Up to an inch: 48%最多一英寸：48%
  • One to three inches: 34%一到三英寸：34%
  • More than three inches: 7%超过三英寸：7%

This is an appropriate and more realistic way of answering the "when" question because of what I call Vacanti's Verity: "When making a forecast (predicting the future), you must accept that there is more than one possible outcome."

这是回答「什么时候」问题的恰当且更现实的方式，因为我称之为 Vacanti 定律的道理：「做预测（预测未来）时，你必须接受存在不止一种可能的结果。」

Unless your team is doing CRUD (Create, Read, Update, and Delete) work in the same system for the 100th time, the delivery time is unknown. However, unknown doesn't mean unpredictable. Just how predictable your delivery system is will be conveyed in the probabilistic forecast, for which we'll use actual delivery data. Because we're concerned with determining delivery time (elapsed time between start and finish) of work, we'll collect start and end dates for our work items.

除非你的团队在同一个系统里第 100 次做 CRUD（创建、读取、更新、删除）工作，否则交付时间是未知的。然而，未知不意味着不可预测。你的交付系统有多可预测将在概率预测中传达，我们会用实际交付数据来做。因为我们关心的是确定工作的交付时间（从开始到完成的经过时间），我们会收集工作项的开始和结束日期。

— 第 95 页 —

You can track additional data such as work type, but to create our forecast, the pairs of dates are sufficient. We use these dates because within them are all the factors that affect delivery time and not only effort: blockers, rework, and work in progress to name a few. And it's because of these other system factors (which represent up to 85% or more of the total elapsed time) that our work items need not be the same size in order to forecast.

你可以跟踪额外的数据如工作类型，但要创建预测，日期对就足够了。我们用这些日期是因为它们包含了影响交付时间的所有因素，而不只是工作量：阻塞、返工、在途工作等。正是因为这些其他系统因素（占总经过时间的 85% 或更多），我们的工作项不需要大小一致就能预测。

When we think probabilistically, we have real power—real as in the real thing, and not guesswork!—with which to plan and communicate with customers and others. Not only do we spend no time estimating, we can provide our customers with objective likely outcomes with which to make economic decisions. We know at any given time the answer to the question "When will it be done?" by running a Monte Carlo simulation of future outcomes.

当我们用概率思考时，我们拥有真正的力量——真的是真家伙，不是瞎猜！——可以用来计划和与客户及其他人沟通。我们不仅不花时间估算，还能给客户提供客观的可能结果来做经济决策。通过运行未来结果的蒙特卡洛模拟，我们在任何时候都知道「什么时候能做完？」的答案。

This simulation (available in open source and pay options) basically uses our delivery-time data to generate all of those possible scenarios, from best to worst case and everything in between.

这个模拟（有开源和付费选项）基本上用我们的交付时间数据来生成所有可能的场景，从最好到最坏以及中间的一切。

The result of a Monte Carlo simulation is a range of outcomes, with a percentage confidence at each. This allows us planning flexibility based on risk tolerance: for a very conservative, risk-averse need, we would use the 95th percentile, which tells us that 95% of the time, we expect to complete the given work, say, 42 work items in 25 days or less. If we're waiting to launch a marketing campaign, we might choose this confidence interval (or perhaps 85th). But if we're heading toward a fixed-date event with high reward potential—for instance, Apple's next announcement of a new watch—it might be worth it to "roll the dice" at the 75th or even 50th percentile. Planning now becomes a business decision based on risk. Also, it reduces stress and harmful pressures that influence the delivery team to (consciously or unconsciously) estimate in ways that can negatively affect their behavior and/or a trustful relationship with the customer. Further, it helps avoid the problem of estimates tending to lock us into initial solutions and bias us against discarding them in favor of better ones.

蒙特卡洛模拟的结果是一系列结果范围，每个都有百分比置信度。这让我们可以根据风险承受能力灵活计划：对于非常保守、风险厌恶的需求，我们会用第 95 百分位，它告诉我们 95% 的情况下，我们预计在 25 天或更短时间内完成给定的 42 个工作项。如果我们在等一个营销活动上线，我们可能选这个置信区间（或者第 85）。但如果我们在冲向一个有高回报潜力的固定日期事件——比如苹果的下一次新手表发布——在第 75 甚至第 50 百分位「掷骰子」可能值得。计划现在变成了基于风险的业务决策。而且它减少了压力和有害的催促，这些压力会影响交付团队（有意识或无意识地）以可能负面影响他们行为和/或与客户信任关系的方式估算。此外，它还有助避免估算把我们锁定在初始方案中、让我们偏向不放弃它们去选更好方案的问题。

Answering the question for any particular piece of work is similarly simple. We just use our data to find our confidence intervals; for instance, we can graphically display this using a scatterplot chart showing delivery times for individual work items over time. We then look at our confidence intervals, drawn at the points where 95% of our items are below the line, 85% of them, and so on, and make the confident claim that "any next item is 85% likely to finish in 15 days or less."

回答任何特定工作的问题同样简单。我们只用数据找到置信区间；例如，我们可以用散点图图形化展示单个工作项随时间的交付时间。然后我们看置信区间线——95% 的项在线以下的点、85% 的点等等——然后自信地说：「下一个项有 85% 的概率在 15 天或更短时间内完成。」
